797.name: segment
797.description: A segment is a sub-group of a segmentation.

6660.name: created_at
6660.description: When the notification of the open was received

826.name: open
826.description:
An open is the act of displaying the content of a broadcast.
For mailings, it is typically captured by adding to the broadcast content an image stored in a system that counts requests to that image, which may not capture all actual opens (if the recipient does not display images).

6566.name: started_at
6566.description:
For a recurring donation, when the donation started.
For a one-off donation, when it is received.

6567.name: total_amount
6567.description: Amount sum of all successful payments

6569.name: ended_at
6569.description:
For a recurring donation, when it stopped.
For a one-off donation, undefined.

6570.name: original_amount
6570.description: The amount of the donation in the original currency

6572.name: frequency_unit
6572.description: one-off for a one-off donation, month for a recurring donation

6575.name: payment_count
6575.description: Number of successful payments for this donation

6576.name: original_currency
6576.description: The currency in which the donation is made

6577.name: payment_method
6577.description:
How the donation is paid.
Sepa (aka direct debit) is a transfer initiated by the organisation on request of the donor, while a bank_transfer is a transfer initated by the donor.

6884.name: fail_count
6884.description: Number of failed payments for this donation

6622.name: amount
6622.description: Amount of the donation converted into the organisation currency

815.name: donation
815.description:
A donation a type of action: it is the intent from a person to give money to the organisation, either once or periodically. The intent may or may not be eventually fulfilled.
N.B.: The campaign associated to a donation (through action and action page) is not the campaign for which the money should be used, but rather the campaign that led the person to donate.

6882.name: language
6882.description: Language of the page in locale format (xx_YY where xx is language code and YY is country code)

6879.name: action_type
6879.description:
Kind of engagement that users can do on the action page.
The type consent is listed here for technical reasons, consents are not considered as actions and are recorded in the consent table.

861.name: action_page
861.description: An action page is a place (such as a web page or a form) written in a given language where we want people to perform actions of a given type. An action page is always associated to a campaign.

862.name: broadcast_metric
862.description: A broadcast metric is an indicator of how recipients interacted with the broadcast. In this table, the value of each metric is given for a specific contact segment (which may be the "everyone" segment).

6521.name: segmentation_id
6521.description: this is necessary to have one segment per segmentation enforced for a contact.

6523.name: left_at
6523.description:
When the contact left the segment, or NULL if the contact is still in the segment.
It is equal to the joined_at column for the next segment within this segmentation.

6524.name: trigger_action_id
6524.description: If applicable, the id of the action that made the contact join the segment

6525.name: joined_at
6525.description:
When the contact joined the segment.
If the contact was in the segment several times, there are several records.

805.name: contact_segment
805.description: A contact_segment record is a link between a person and a segment.

6981.name: shared_source_id
6981.description: Utm parameters used in the shared URL

6605.name: share_count
6605.description:
is this a count of shares people did on the journey when converting ?  <- i think it's this
Or shares within social media?

6606.name: new_member_count
6606.description: Number of people who became members of the organisation directly thanks to this share

6607.name: conversion_count
6607.description: Number of people who took action directly thanks this share

800.name: share
800.description:
A share is a type of action: it is the act of referring an action page to other people.
A share is associated to 2 source records: the one that led to the share action (the action source), and the one that will be the source of any action coming from that share (the shared source).

6662.name: broadcast_id
6662.description: The broadcast from which the contact sent the unsubscribe request

6664.name: created_at
6664.description: When te unsubscribe request was received

827.name: unsub
827.description:
An unsub is the request from a broadcast recipient not to receive further broadcasts anymore. 
While people may send such a request through different means, an unsub refers specifically to the act of using one of the unsuscribe options that are mandatory in any mass communication.

6977.name: status
6977.description:
One of:
 - accepted: the person became a member
 - rejected: the person refused to become a member
 - pending: the person was asked asynchronously (eg by email) to become a member
 - cancelled: the person withdrew their consent

7137.name: trigger_action_id
7137.description: The action that led to this consent event

7133.name: source_id
7133.description: The utm parameters that led to this consent.

870.name: consent
870.description:
In this database, a consent is either any event regarding a person's explicit consent to have their personal data processed or used for a certain purpose.
It may be an asynchronous consent ask, an asynchronous consent response, a synchronous consent ask and response, or an unsollicited consent cancellation.

807.name: source
807.description: A source is a set of so-called utm parameters that can be used to identify how someone got exposed to a link. It is a major mechanism of action attribution.

6624.name: sent_at
6624.description: When the sending of the broadcast started

7069.name: language
7069.description: The language in which the broadcast was written, in locale format (xx_YY).

809.name: broadcast
809.description: A broadcast is a way to direct people to action pages, using group / mass communication.

6504.name: preferred_language
6504.description: The language used to communicate with the contact, in locale format (xx_YY)

6505.name: email_domain
6505.description: The part after the @ in the primary email address of the contact

6507.name: created_at
6507.description: When the contact was added to our database

6509.name: country
6509.description:
The 2-letter country code of the contact.
What this country represents is up to the contact (place of birth, place of living, etc).

6497.name: campaign_type
6497.description:
One of the following:
 - wemove: a "regular" campaign run by the organisation
 - youmove: a campaign initiated by a citizen or organisation on the Youmove platform
 - eci: European Citizen Initiative
 - trial: a campaign run the organisation to assess its potential success

6495.name: name
6495.description: The internal name of the campaign

811.name: campaign
811.description:
In the context of analytics, a campaign is a "project" with a political and/or organisational goal. It is the primary concept used to focus data analysis to a specific area or goal. 
N.B.: It may be different from what your action tool or CRM may refer to as campaign, which is rather a technical definition and is closer to the analytics concept of action page.

812.name: segmentation
812.description:
A segmentation is a way split a group of people into different segments (sub-groups).
This split is a partition: each person of the base group is attributed to exactly one segment (everyone is in a segment, no-one is in more than one segment).

6873.name: source_id
6873.description: The utm parameters that led to this action

6872.name: created_at
6872.description: When the contact did the action

6876.name: action_page_id
6876.description:
The action page where the action was done.
Attributes a type, language and campaign to the action.

813.name: action
813.description: An action is what a single person does on an action page, a specific engagement act performed by a person. It is therefore the link between a contact and an action page.

814.name: click
814.description:
A click is the act of opening a link in a broadcast.
The information is obtained by using an intermediary system that identifies and redirects recipients to the destination URL after capturing each click event.

6591.name: status
6591.description:
One of:
 - success: the payment was processed
 - fail: the payment could not be processed
 - cancel: the payment was processed but the donor requested to take it back

819.name: payment
819.description: A payment is an attempt (successful or failed) to fulfill a donation.

7062.name: sent_at
7062.description: When the sending of the broadcast started

7070.name: language
7070.description: The language in which the broadcast was written, in locale format (xx_YY).

6657.name: sent_at
6657.description: When the sending of the test started

6653.name: created_at
6653.description: When the test was created in database

825.name: broadcast_test
825.description: A broadcast test is a set of broadcasts sent at the same time but to different people, meant to be compared to each other to identify the one that performs best. It is also known as an A/B test or A/B/n test.

7082.name: metric
7082.description:
One of the following:
 - recipients: number of broadcast recipients targeted by the campaign
 - messages: total number of broadcast messages (emails, sms, etc) sent for the campaign
 - unsubs: number of people who unsubscribed through a broadcast of the campaign
 - actions: total number of actions of any type attributed to the campaign
 - new_members: total number of people who subscribed to the organisation mailing list thanks to the campaign
 - activated: number of people who joined the active members'segment via an action linked to the campaign
 - shares: number of actions of type share associated to the campaign
 - donations_total_amount: total amount of money (one-off and recurring total) fundraised via the campaign

890.name: campaign_metric
890.description: A campaign metric is a indicator of how people interacted with the campaign. In this table, the value of each metric is given for a specific contact segment (which may be the "everyone" segment).

7095.name: name
7095.description: The internal name of the campaign

7096.name: campaign_type
7096.description:
One of the following:
 - wemove: a "regular" campaign run by the organisation
 - youmove: a campaign initiated by a citizen or organisation on the Youmove platform
 - eci: European Citizen Initiative
 - trial: a campaign run the organisation to assess its potential success

6649.name: url
6649.description:
Complete target URL of the link, including utm parameters.
This is not the URL of the click tracking system.

6650.name: source_id
6650.description: utm parameters that were used in the URL

828.name: broadcast_link
828.description:
A broadcast link is a web link found in the content of a broadcast.
It is associated to the source that matches the utm parameters used in the link, which can be used to attribute actions to a broadcast.

items.name: Consents
items.description: Number of consents for each status

native.query:
SELECT 
    SUBSTR(l.name, 1, 6) AS version, c.status AS consent_status, COUNT(*) AS `count`
FROM consent c
JOIN (
    SELECT 
        broadcast.name, contact_id, MAX(created_at) latest 
    FROM broadcast
    JOIN broadcast_link link ON link.broadcast_id=broadcast.id
    JOIN source s ON s.id = link.source_id
    JOIN consent ON consent.source_id=s.id
    WHERE {{broadcast_test_id}}
    GROUP BY broadcast.id, contact_id
) l ON l.contact_id=c.contact_id AND l.latest=c.created_at
GROUP BY version, consent_status

items.name: Count of accepted consents without a member join

native.query:
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM segment s
JOIN consent c ON c.status = 'accepted'
LEFT JOIN contact_segment cs ON cs.segment_id = s.id AND c.contact_id = cs.contact_id AND ABS(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, c.created_at, cs.joined_at)) <= 60
WHERE s.name='Member' AND cs.id IS NULL

items.name: Count of accepted consents without a member join, over time

native.query:
SELECT DATE_FORMAT(c.created_at, '%Y-%m') AS consent_month, COUNT(*)
FROM segment s
JOIN consent c ON c.status = 'accepted'
LEFT JOIN contact_segment cs ON cs.segment_id = s.id AND c.contact_id = cs.contact_id AND ABS(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, c.created_at, cs.joined_at)) <= 60
WHERE s.name='Member' AND cs.id IS NULL
GROUP BY consent_month

card.name: Random pick of member joins without an accepted consent

native.query:
SELECT contact.id, contact.created_at AS contact_created_at, contact.country, contact.preferred_language, cs.joined_at, CONCAT('https://www.wemove.eu/civicrm/contact/view?cid=', contact.id) AS crm_url
FROM segment s
JOIN contact_segment cs ON cs.segment_id = s.id
JOIN contact ON contact.id = cs.contact_id
LEFT JOIN consent c ON c.contact_id = cs.contact_id AND ABS(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, c.created_at, cs.joined_at)) <= 60 AND c.status = 'accepted'
WHERE s.name='Member' AND c.id IS NULL
ORDER BY RAND() LIMIT 5

card.name: Random pick of accepted consents without a member join

native.query:
SELECT contact.id, contact.created_at AS contact_created_at, contact.country, contact.preferred_language, c.created_at AS consent_date, CONCAT('https://www.wemove.eu/civicrm/contact/view?cid=', contact.id) AS crm_url
FROM segment s
JOIN consent c ON c.status = 'accepted'
JOIN contact ON contact.id = c.contact_id
LEFT JOIN contact_segment cs ON cs.segment_id = s.id AND c.contact_id = cs.contact_id AND ABS(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, c.created_at, cs.joined_at)) <= 60
WHERE s.name='Member' AND cs.id IS NULL
ORDER BY RAND() LIMIT 5

card.name: Random pick of member leaves without a cancelled consent

native.query:
SELECT contact.id, contact.created_at AS contact_created_at, contact.country, contact.preferred_language, cs.left_at, CONCAT('https://www.wemove.eu/civicrm/contact/view?cid=', contact.id) AS crm_url
FROM segment s
JOIN contact_segment cs ON cs.segment_id = s.id AND cs.left_at IS NOT NULL
JOIN contact ON contact.id = cs.contact_id
LEFT JOIN consent c ON c.contact_id = cs.contact_id AND ABS(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, c.created_at, cs.left_at)) <= 60 AND c.status = 'cancelled'
WHERE s.name='Member' AND c.id IS NULL
ORDER BY RAND() LIMIT 5

card.name: Random pick of cancelled consents without a member leave

native.query:
SELECT contact.id, contact.created_at AS contact_created_at, contact.country, contact.preferred_language, c.created_at AS cancel_date, CONCAT('https://www.wemove.eu/civicrm/contact/view?cid=', contact.id) AS crm_url
FROM segment s
JOIN consent c ON c.status = 'cancelled'
JOIN contact ON contact.id = c.contact_id
LEFT JOIN contact_segment cs ON cs.segment_id = s.id AND c.contact_id = cs.contact_id AND ABS(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, c.created_at, cs.left_at)) <= 60
WHERE s.name='Member' AND cs.id IS NULL
ORDER BY RAND() LIMIT 5

items.description: Number of people who clicked a link versus number of people who displayed the open tracker.

native.query:
SELECT 
    c.status, COUNT(*) AS `count`
FROM consent c
JOIN (
    SELECT 
        contact_id, MAX(created_at) latest 
    FROM broadcast_link
    JOIN source s ON s.id = broadcast_link.source_id
    JOIN consent ON consent.source_id=s.id
    WHERE {{broadcast_id}}
    GROUP BY contact_id
) l ON l.contact_id=c.contact_id AND l.latest=c.created_at
GROUP BY status
